pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Optional semicolon ambiguity after return or leading expression
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A newline can change which statement JavaScript parses, especially after return or before a line beginning with ( or [.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Automatic semicolon insertion is not a simple newline rule. Restricted productions and continuation parsing can produce valid code with unintended meaning.
where_it_appears: IIFEs or array literals after another statement
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Line break appears at a syntactically sensitive location and no explicit semicolon prevents continuation or restricted-production insertion.
conditions_required: Semicolons omitted or generated code concatenated
A following line starts with (, [, /, +, or -
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape:
return
{ ok: true } or const x = f
(a+b).toString()
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The source layout looks like two separate statements to a human but the parser sees one continuation or an inserted semicolon.
prevention_or_mitigation: Keep return value on same line
checks_or_diagnostics: Search for restricted keywords followed by newline
Search for semicolonless lines followed by leading ( or [
Add a tiny runtime test for affected function

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Implicit coercion in comparisons, arithmetic, and output
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Values from forms, query strings, CSV, JSON, or DOM attributes arrive as strings and then participate in numeric or boolean logic.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: JavaScript applies different conversions for equality, relational comparison, +, other arithmetic, truthiness, and object-to-primitive conversion.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Boundary values are used before explicit normalization.
conditions_required: Operators or conditionals are applied directly
Tests cover only happy numeric path
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: const total = formValue + 1; if (count) save(count); if (x == y) ...
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: JavaScript operator overloading and coercion are convenient in demos but dangerous when inputs cross runtime/API boundaries.
prevention_or_mitigation: Parse and validate at the boundary
Use ?? instead of || for nullish defaults
checks_or_diagnostics: List every operator applied before normalization

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Loose equality or relational comparison accepts unintended values
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Comparison appears to compare two values directly but first applies JavaScript conversion rules.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: == and != perform loose equality conversions. Relational operators may compare as strings or numbers depending on operands and conversion.
symptoms: Lexicographic order where numeric order expected
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code uses loose comparison or relational comparison before type normalization.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: if (id == input) ...; items.sort((a,b) => a.value > b.value)
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The expression is visually simple and often works for one test value.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use explicit parsing and comparator functions

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Null or undefined reaches a property access
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A nested object is missing on one path and the next property read or method call throws.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Property access on null or undefined raises TypeError. Optional chaining changes the failure into undefined but does not validate required data.
symptoms: Later undefined or NaN instead of early failure
Fallback used for valid falsy value
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code assumes a value exists because it exists in the common path.
conditions_required: At least one branch/API result can omit the object
Tests do not cover missing object
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: user.profile.name or document.querySelector(sel).textContent without null check
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: JavaScript lets missing object properties return undefined, so the failure appears one step later at nested access.
checks_or_diagnostics: Trace source of each base object
Test absent parent, present null, and present value

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Shared object or array mutation leaks across callers
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A helper mutates an object/array that another part of the program still owns.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Object and array assignments copy references. Mutating methods and property writes affect all aliases to the same object.
symptoms: UI or API response changes unexpectedly
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Reference aliasing is not considered when writing mutating code.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: function addTag(item){ item.tags.push("x"); return item; }
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: const gives a false sense of immutability, and shallow spread only copies one level.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use immutable update patterns where safe
checks_or_diagnostics: Search for mutating array methods and property writes

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Prototype chain hides ownership mistakes
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A property appears to exist because it is inherited, or an own property shadows inherited behavior.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Property reads traverse prototypes. for/in and in include inherited properties, while Object.keys and Object.hasOwn focus on own/enumerable properties.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Ownership and inheritance are not distinguished.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: if (key in obj) accept(obj[key]); or obj.method = ... shadows prototype method
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: JavaScript objects are not just flat dictionaries.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use Map or Object.create(null) for dictionaries when appropriate

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Sparse array holes behave differently from undefined elements
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Array length suggests elements exist, but callbacks or serialization treat holes specially.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Sparse arrays have missing indexed properties. Many array methods skip holes; JSON may represent holes in arrays differently than object undefined properties.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code equates array length with count of present values.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: Array(3).map(fn) or delete rows[1]; rows.forEach(process)
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: A hole displays similarly to undefined in some tools but is a different property state.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use splice instead of delete for removal
checks_or_diagnostics: Use i in arr to detect holes

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Array-like object is treated as a real array
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A collection has length and indexes but not Array methods or array iteration guarantees.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Array-like and iterable are distinct. Host objects can have special live/static behavior and may need Array.from before array methods.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code assumes length plus indexes means Array instance.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: nodes.map(fn) where nodes is a DOM collection
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The object prints like a list in devtools but has a different prototype and lifecycle.

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: this binding changes when method is passed around
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A method that works as obj.method() fails when used as a callback or standalone function.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: this is determined by invocation form for ordinary functions. Arrow functions capture lexical this and do not create their own dynamic receiver.
symptoms: Method works in direct call only
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Function depends on receiver but call site loses receiver.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: const m = obj.method; m(); setTimeout(obj.method, 0)
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The method name still looks attached to the object in source even when the value has been extracted.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use arrow only for lexical this
Avoid this-dependent functions as bare callbacks

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Closure captures changing or long-lived state
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A returned or delayed function observes state that has changed since the function was created.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Closures retain lexical bindings. Captured objects remain mutable and long-lived closures can extend object lifetime.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Captured binding is shared across invocations or mutated after capture.
conditions_required: Outer variable reassigned or object mutated
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: let count = 0; return () => ++count; or callbacks capture mutable config
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The source visually hides that the variable outlives the outer call.
checks_or_diagnostics: Test repeated calls and concurrent callbacks

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Class syntax hides prototype semantics
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A reviewer treats class methods as instance data or forgets that class behavior still uses prototypes and this.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: class creates constructor/prototype-based objects. Prototype methods are shared; instance fields or arrow methods are own per instance. super and subclassing depend on prototype relationships.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Class syntax is read as classical object model without checking JavaScript-specific method placement and this binding.
conditions_required: Methods moved between prototype and instance
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: class C { m(){} } vs class C { m = () => {} }
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The syntax resembles class-based languages but retains JavaScript prototypes.
prevention_or_mitigation: Choose prototype methods by default unless lexical this/identity needed

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: CommonJS ES module or loader mismatch
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A file is written for one module system but executed by another loader or transform path.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: ES modules and CommonJS differ in syntax, strictness, binding/export shapes, loading configuration, and interop. Browser, Node, bundler, and test runner loaders differ.
symptoms: Works in build but not direct runtime
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Module format, file extension, package config, or bundler/test transform is inconsistent.
conditions_required: Package type or file extension changes
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: const x = require("m") in ESM; import x from CommonJS without adapter
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The imported name often looks correct even when the actual object shape differs.
prevention_or_mitigation: Choose one module system per boundary
checks_or_diagnostics: Run minimal import/require probe in target runtime

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: JSON serialization drops or changes values
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Data crossing JSON loses JavaScript-specific values and behavior.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: JSON.stringify omits or transforms unsupported values and JSON.parse returns plain data without prototypes unless reviver logic handles it.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code treats JSON as a deep clone or exact serialization of JavaScript objects.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(objWithDateMapUndefined))
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The output is valid JSON, so the loss may not look like an error.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use explicit schema and custom serialization
Avoid JSON clone for complex objects
checks_or_diagnostics: Test undefined, Date, Map, Set, Error, NaN, Infinity, cycle

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Date/timezone confusion
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Date code changes meaning across timezone, locale, or parse context.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Date stores instants but constructors, parsing, and getters can use local timezone or UTC. String formats and display methods have different assumptions.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Code does not distinguish instant, local date, formatted string, and timezone-aware display.
conditions_required: Tests run in one timezone only
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: new Date("2020-01-01").getDate() or date.toString() used for storage
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Date values print as readable strings that hide timezone conversions.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use explicit ISO instants with timezone for instants
Store local dates separately from timestamps

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Regular expression overmatches or undermatches input
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A regex used for validation or parsing accepts invalid input or rejects valid input.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Pattern flags, anchors, greediness, Unicode handling, escaping, global state, and lastIndex affect matching.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Regex is used as if it represented a full grammar and all edge cases.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: /\d+/.test("abc123def") as full numeric validation
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Regex success often means substring match, not whole-input validity.
checks_or_diagnostics: Test empty, multiline, Unicode, long, invalid, and malicious-like inputs

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Unhandled Promise rejection
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: An async operation fails and no code awaits/catches/reports it reliably.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Promise rejections propagate through chains until handled. Fire-and-forget promises need explicit reporting policy. async functions return rejected promises when they throw.
symptoms: UI keeps loading or silently ignores error
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Promise-returning call is started but not returned, awaited, or caught.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: doWork(); // promise ignored or async function handler(){ failingCall(); }
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The function call syntax looks synchronous even though failure is delivered later.
prevention_or_mitigation: Mark intentional background work and attach reporting
checks_or_diagnostics: Assert async test waits for failure

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: async function returns Promise unexpectedly
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A caller treats an async function as if it returns the resolved value directly.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Every async function returns a Promise, even when returning a non-Promise value. Callers must await or chain it.
symptoms: try/catch does not catch rejection without await
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Synchronous API contract changed by adding async.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: const value = getValueAsync(); if (value) ...
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The body may look sequential due await syntax, hiding the Promise API at the boundary.
prevention_or_mitigation: Do not add async unless API can change
checks_or_diagnostics: Search callers of newly async function

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Callback error path ignored during promise conversion
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: A callback-style API is wrapped or used without handling the documented error branch.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Callback APIs may report errors through an error argument, separate callback, or event. Throwing inside async callback is not the same as rejecting an outer promise.
symptoms: Success handler runs with invalid data
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Wrapper resolves success but forgets reject path or multiple-settle guard.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: new Promise(resolve => api((err,data)=> resolve(data)))
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The happy-path wrapper is short and appears correct until the API fails.
prevention_or_mitigation: Prefer built-in Promise APIs when available and verified

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Browser API used in Node or Node API used in browser
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Host-specific global or module is referenced in the wrong runtime.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: ECMAScript core does not include DOM, fs, process, Buffer, or many other host APIs. Browsers and Node provide different host environments.
symptoms: fs not found in browser bundle
works in Jest but fails in browser
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: File role and execution runtime are not identified before review/refactor.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: import fs from "fs" in frontend code or document.querySelector in Node script
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: All files are JavaScript, so environment differences are easy to miss.
checks_or_diagnostics: Search for browser and Node globals

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: DOM event assumptions break UI behavior
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Event code assumes target, timing, default action, or listener lifecycle incorrectly.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Browser event dispatch includes propagation, default actions, listener options, target/currentTarget distinctions, and async interaction with rendering/user input.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Event lifecycle and propagation are not modeled.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: container.addEventListener("click", e => e.target.value)
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Events look like simple callbacks but carry browser-specific dispatch semantics.

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Fetch/networking success assumption
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Networking code assumes a fulfilled promise equals successful parsed data.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Fetch-style APIs and host networking have separate network, HTTP status, body parsing, CORS/security, abort, timeout, and application error concerns. Current behavior must be verified for the target environment.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Only the happy path is modeled.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: const data = await fetch(url).then(r => r.json())
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The promise API hides multiple failure layers behind one await expression.

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Browser storage treated as durable secure database
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Client storage is used without considering quota, lifetime, privacy, origin, or security.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Browser storage APIs are host features with evolving privacy/security/quota behavior. They are not ECMAScript core and must be verified for current platform and deployment.
symptoms: Data missing in private mode or after policy change
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Storage API chosen without threat model or current support check.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: localStorage.setItem("token", secret) or large JSON cache without quota handling
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The API looks like a simple key/value map but has browser policy and security constraints.
prevention_or_mitigation: Do not store secrets in ordinary client storage

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Worker message boundary identity assumption
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Main and worker code assume sent objects remain shared ordinary objects.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Worker communication uses host message passing and cloning/transfer rules. Mutation, methods, prototypes, and transferable ownership may not behave like local references.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Message boundary is treated like a synchronous function call or shared object reference.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: worker.postMessage(obj); obj.changed = true; expect worker to see change
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Both sides use JavaScript objects, but the boundary is not ordinary reference passing.

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Node stream lifecycle ignored
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Stream code handles chunks but not completion, errors, or backpressure.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Node streams are asynchronous data sources/sinks with data/end/error/close/finish/backpressure behavior. APIs evolve and should be verified for current Node.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Stream is treated as a complete buffer.
conditions_required: Only data handler or write calls present
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: stream.on("data", chunk => chunks.push(chunk)); return chunks.join("")
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Data chunks arrive over time and completion is a separate event/state.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use buffered read only for bounded input

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Child process or worker chosen without boundary plan
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Parallel/external execution is added without accounting for messaging, lifecycle, security, and deployment support.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Node child processes and worker threads solve different problems and have different data, CPU, OS, security, and lifecycle behavior. Browser workers differ again.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Execution boundary choice is made before defining workload, data flow, and trust boundary.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: exec(`tool ${userInput}`) or worker for small trivial task
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: The API can look like a performance shortcut while adding a new failure domain.
prevention_or_mitigation: Choose worker for CPU-bound JS; child process for trusted external program when deployment allows
Sanitize shell input or avoid shell

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Tooling or transpilation mismatch
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: The code reviewed is not the code executed because a tool transforms it or a runtime target differs.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Bundlers, Babel, JSX transforms, test environments, linters, and package managers can change syntax support, module loading, globals, and output shape.
symptoms: Works in dev but fails in production
Tests pass with transform missing in runtime
Syntax accepted by build but not runtime
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Tool configuration and runtime target are not part of the review.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: Syntax supported by Babel in tests but not by deployed Node/browser without transform
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: Tools make non-native code appear normal in source.
checks_or_diagnostics: Compare source and emitted code for suspect file

pitfalls_and_failure_modes.pitfall_or_failure_name: Apps Script runtime confused with browser or Node
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.plain_language_description: Apps Script project code is reviewed as if every JavaScript file has the same APIs and lifecycle.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.technical_description: Apps Script server-side functions, HtmlService client HTML, triggers, Google services, quotas, scopes, and deployment behavior are Apps Script platform features outside the book.
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.root_cause_pattern: Files are not classified by Apps Script runtime role and current docs are not checked.
conditions_required: Platform behavior claimed without current docs
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.minimal_example_shape: Client HTML calls SpreadsheetApp directly or server .gs calls document.querySelector
pitfalls_and_failure_modes.why_it_surprises_developers: All pieces are JavaScript-like, but they execute in different hosts with different services.
prevention_or_mitigation: Verify current Google docs for every service/trigger/quota/scope
Use explicit client/server message data shapes
checks_or_diagnostics: Which file runs in browser vs server?
Which service APIs and scopes are used?
What current docs prove quota/deployment behavior?
